alignments.note: The bare accusative מַרְבַדִּים rendered *carpets of tapestry* as one nominal phrase; head on the word carrying the lexeme (rule 31).

The English verb reaches the Hebrew's bare second accusative through the supplied *with*, which joins the verb's unit (rule 44, as in *daubed ... with untempered mortar*); the unit is discontinuous under rule 25.
Bare nominal in a gapped line with a supplied preposition (rule 33); head on the lexeme-bearing word, *cloths* being the generic (rule 31).
Rectum takes the *of*; the construct also takes a supplied *the* (rules 19 and 29).

review_notes: *of tapestry* was kept inside מַרְבַדִּים's own rendering rather than marked added; treating it as supplied English was the competing reading.
The margin's *Or, cushions* was read and set aside (rule 38).
